title: Fitting a fireplace surround to a chimney breast
subtitle: Fix a timber or MDF fireplace surround to a chimney breast wall, level and plumb, ready for a hearth and a back panel or board
excerpt: How to fit a timber or MDF fireplace surround to a chimney breast. Covers finding and marking the chimney breast centre, levelling the surround, fixing to the wall, and fitting the hearth and back board.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). Reader's Digest Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK Building Regulations Part J guidance on hearth construction (open access).

glossaryTerms.definition: The masonry or timber-framed projection that houses the flue from a fireplace. The fireplace opening sits in the breast; the surround frames the opening. Not all chimney breasts contain working flues; many have been blocked up.

The base slab of non-combustible material (concrete, stone, or tile on a concrete bed) that forms the floor of the fireplace opening and extends in front of it. Building Regulations Part J require a minimum depth and projection from the opening for any solid fuel or gas appliance.

content.text: A fireplace surround fits to the face of the

wall around the opening. The surround is centred on the opening, held level and plumb, and screwed to the wall through wall plugs. The hearth sits in front. This tutorial covers a decorative (non-functional) or gas-fire context; work with Gas Safe registered engineers for any gas appliance connection.

Fitting the surround is domestic DIY. Connecting a gas fire or gas log-effect unit to the gas supply must be done by a Gas Safe registered engineer. Any new solid-fuel burning appliance must comply with Building Regulations Part J and be notified to your local authority. The surround fitting itself does not require notification.
Mark the centre line and check the opening

Find the centre of the fireplace opening by measuring its width and marking the midpoint on the wall above. Drop a plumb line or use a long spirit level to transfer the centre point to the floor. The surround legs should sit at equal distances either side of this line. Check that the wall face is flat; any lump or hollow behind the surround's fixing points will need to be cut back or packed with a wooden shim.
Hold the surround against the wall with the legs on the floor or on the

surface. Check that the top rail is level with a spirit level. Shim under the legs if necessary to bring the surround level and plumb. Mark the wall through the fixing lugs or brackets on the back of the surround.
Drill and fix to the wall

Step 1 on a masonry chimney breast: check the wall with a cable-and-pipe detector before drilling. Drill the fixing points with a 10 mm masonry bit using the SDS drill. Insert wall plugs and reposition the surround. Drive the fixing screws through the surround's lugs or brackets into the plugs. Tighten until the surround sits firm against the wall. Any gap between the surround back and the wall face is filled with decorator's caulk applied in a thin bead and smoothed.
Fit the back board and hearth

A decorative back panel (usually MDF with a fireplace-effect paint or a tiled panel) sits in the opening behind the surround. Measure the opening carefully; most back panels are sold to standard sizes. Fix lightly with mirror adhesive or a few small screws through a batten at the top. The hearth tile or stone is laid on a solid concrete sub-base; the hearth for a decorative or electric fire sits on the existing floor surface and is held in position by its own weight.

attrs.symptom: The surround leans slightly forward or back from the wall
attrs.cause: The chimney breast face is not flush with the surrounding wall, or the surround back is slightly bowed.
attrs.fix: Pack behind the high points of the surround with thin plywood shims. Fill any remaining gap at the wall joint with decorator's caulk.

attrs.symptom: The surround is level but looks misaligned with the opening
attrs.cause: The opening itself is not centred on the chimney breast.
attrs.fix: Recentre the surround on the opening rather than on the breast face, adjusting the fixing positions accordingly.
